text:
Rae: dropped a new pass on the spend pane — paying special attention to invoice action grouping and token breakdown density. figma: https://www.figma.com/file/zzz-spend-pane. PTAL.
Ben: First glance looks promising. Quick callout: per-invoice CTAs are crowding the row on <1024px. Could we collapse less-frequent actions into an overflow menu?
Isha: yes to overflow. For power users we still need bulk actions visible when multiple rows are selected. Suggest sticky footer bulk actions when selection > 0.
Miles: sticky footer is good for mobile, but on desktop it feels odd. How about header bulk action + sticky footer on touch devices? We can A/B it.
Carmen: Accessibility nit: overflow menus must be keyboard operable and announce their open/close. Also add `aria-label` to each download action e.g. `aria-label=\"Download invoice PDF 2024-07-01-INV-987\"`.
A11yBot: scan: legend contrast low on compact mode; overflow toggle missing `aria-expanded`; bulk button lacks `aria-hidden` toggle when hidden.
Rae: noted — will update tokens and aria attributes. Also microcopy: change "Download" -> "Download PDF invoice" and surface "Export CSV ledger" as a second option in header.
Ben: token breakdown: don't mix units. If we must show tokens + USD, make the cost a secondary inline metric with a smaller font or show a toggle. Combined axes confused users in research.
Isha: agree. Prefer a toggle between metrics or a split view. For narrow widths show the unit chip next to the value (e.g., "1.3M • tokens").
Miles: small UX: move numeric units out of the y-axis and inline next to numbers to save room. Also shorten big numbers (2.4M) at <600px. Full number on hover/focus.
Carmen: also ensure focus ring is 3px and uses accessible color. And add `aria-live` announcements for bulk-download completion/failure.
Rae: will: 1) push changes to figma (overflow + header-bulk/ sticky-footer variants), 2) update microcopy and aria patterns in spec, 3) add telemetry keys `billing.bulk_download.triggered` with `placement` and `billing.denom.toggle`.
Ben: sounds good. If you can drop both header-left and header-right mockups I'll throw them into the A/B slate.
Isha: one more — remember last-used scope per-user as default. That reduced confusion during usability tests.
Rae: noted, last-used first, then role fallback. I'll post updated frames by tomorrow AM. Thanks team :thumbsup:
Carmen: thanks!
